# dsh-session-map
English | 中文
Adds a third tab to the DSH conversation view: **a draggable, zoomable map of your session tree**.
It answers the question the native session list cannot:
> Which message, in which conversation, did this thread branch off from — and how many branches hang
ssage, in which conversation, did this thread branch off from — and how many branches hang under it?
The native list is **a line**. Parent/child shows up as indentation, and once a tree has several bra
nches the children all look the same. This plugin draws the tree as **a map**: click a node, you swi
tch to that session.
## What it looks like
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The centre is the **current session** (the focus), the parent sits directly above, and children spre
ad across the **lower semicircle** — the entire upper half is reserved for the parent. That rule is
not just aesthetics: node cards are wide (276 px at the centre), so a child landing at dead-left or
dead-right has its connecting line completely swallowed by the card, and the picture reads as "no li
ne at all". (That was a real defect in v0.1.0, fixed in v0.1.1 — see the regression guard under *Kno
was a real defect in v0.1.0, fixed in v0.1.1 — see the regression guard under *Known limitations*.)
- **Click a node → switch to that session.** (A click that ends a drag does not count, so panning ne

ver switches you by accident.)
- **Whole-tree** toggle lays the entire tree out at once (radial tidy

-tree + layered guide rings).
- **Drag = pan; wheel = zoom anchored at the pointer** (same feel as a

game map). There are also `− / ＋` buttons and a "fit everything" button.
- A breadcrumb across the
top shows the path from the current focus to the root; the right side shows `depth N · M branches`.
- Status dot in each node's upper-right corner: running (cyan) / waiting for you (amber) / done (dim
Status dot in each node's upper-right corner: running (cyan) / waiting for you (amber) / done (dim).
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**After restarting DSH**, the conversation view gains a third tab: **Conversation | Traces | Tree ma
p**. It sits after the two built-in tabs. If you do not see it, the plugin was installed but not mou
nted — check that its name is in `dsh.profile.bundles`.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
This plugin **does not modify any built-in code**. It is purely additive; once removed, the environm
ent is exactly as it was.
## Structure
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Why the host half is empty
`dsh/index.js` exports only `name` / `inject = []` / `apply(_ctx) {}` and does nothing.
There is exactly one reason: the Cordis config tree needs **a resolvable module entry point** for th
e bundle to attach. Every capability this plugin has lives on the UI side; the host side has nothing
to do. So it registers no routes, no services, reads no config — **what it changes = zero**.
### Why the client half looks the way it does
An external plugin's client bundle goes through the DSH shell's **lazy-CJS protocol**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
React **must** come from `require('react')` — the shell's own copy. Bundling your own React means ho
oks cannot see the shell's runtime context.
### Mount point
Registered into the `conversation.view` seat (a **list-type seat**; the built-in UI ships two tabs,
"Conversation" and "Traces"):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Known limitations
Ordered by severity.
- 🔴 **It gets crowded at `n≥5`.** If the centre session has more than 5 direct branches, the lower s
emicircle cannot hold cards that wide and adjacent nodes overlap. The root cause is a geometric hard
limit: cards are 208 px wide, the container is only ~720 px, and 5 cards need 1040 px. **But real d
ata almost never hits this** — across 69 real sessions scanned, a user's own conversation had at mos

t 2 branches; the sessions with many children (e.g. 23) were all subagents.
- 🟠 **Subagent sessions
appear in the tree.** The data-side reason for the previous point: DSH's `useSessions.ids` includes

all 69 sessions, 34 of which are subagents. The plugin currently treats them all alike.
- 🟡 **Whole-
tree view is bounded by window size.** Large trees require zooming out, which shrinks the text — an

inherent cost of a canvas, not a bug. Use focus mode for detail.
- 🟡 **Dragging has no inertia or bo

unds.** The feel is "tracks your hand", not "flings and coasts". Deliberate.
- 🟡 **Only `parentId` i
s honoured.** An empty session whose parent has not been persisted yet shows as "upstream" but canno

t be clicked through; say something inside it and it persists.
- ⚪ **`label` is not localised** — ha

rdcoded English "Tree map".
- ⚪ **No HMR wiring**: editing `client.js` takes effect on page refresh
(the bundle route derives its rev from the content hash). "No DSH restart needed" was measured, not
route derives its rev from the content hash). "No DSH restart needed" was measured, not documented.
### A regression guard
v0.1.0 had a real defect: at `n=2` the children landed at dead-left and dead-right (±90°), and with
`Rx=223` against "centre half-width 138 + child half-width 104 = 242", **the entire connecting line
hid under the cards** — 3 nodes on screen, 0 lines, reading as "feature not implemented". There is n
ow a dedicated assertion guarding it (a `visibleLen` sampling method requiring every centre↔child vi
sible segment to exceed 22 px, scanned over `n=1..4`). Whoever next touches the angles in `layoutFoc
us` will trip it first.
## Other limits, stated plainly
- The virtual root is **a display-only grouping node**, not a session that exists in DSH. It adds on

e node at the "root" level (the real root count is the N written in its title).
- Forking from a sou
rce session with **no completed turn** is rejected by the host (`session/fork-unavailable`); the plu
gin reports this honestly and retries once against the current main session, recording the fallback
rather than hiding it.
